edit.description: `readPhaseTemplate` joins `renderPrompt` on the interface and on the built object — the bytes half of the seam, on the surface a chain actually reads
the groomer case's hand-composed `new URL('../examples/' + promptPath)` read becomes the api's own loader, and the new member's two resolution arms

summary: `FlumeApi` carries `renderPrompt` but not the loader producing the bytes it now takes, so a chain must respell the engine's promptPath resolution to call the one member it has

per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

acceptance: a chain handed `api` loads a phase's prompt template through the api rather than respelling `resolve(configDir, promptPath)` and the namespaced-path fold by hand; the relative-beneath-configDir and absolute-as-given arms are both the engine's answer, and the one measured copy in the suite is deleted in the same commit
tests: a chain loads a phase's prompt template through the api it was handed
the api's prompt-template loader resolves a relative promptPath beneath the chain's config dir
the api's prompt-template loader takes an absolute promptPath as given
notes: 84363656 retired `RenderOptions.promptFile` for `template`, and `src/index.ts:155` states the seam rule — the loader is public beside the renderer. It reached the barrel only: a chain takes every engine value from `api` (`src/flumeApi.ts:1`), so the member it can still call needs bytes it has no engine call for. Measured copy: `tests/examples.test.ts:2855`. No queued entry names either file.
